es: Reconocer cómo se estructura una historia para inspirar, advertir o convencer, y señalar el momento que revela su propósito.

teaching.en: A good story has an arc: a situation, a problem, a turning point and an outcome.
teaching.es: Una buena historia tiene un arco: una situación, un problema, un giro y un desenlace.
teaching.explanationEs: Arc es la forma de la historia; outcome es cómo termina.
segments: A good story has an arc: a situation,
a problem, a turning point and an outcome.
teaching.audioText: A good story has an arc: a situation, a problem, a turning point and an outcome.

teaching.en: A story can inspire: the speaker fails twice, then finds a way, and the audience feels hope.
teaching.es: Una historia puede inspirar: el narrador fracasa dos veces, luego encuentra un camino y la audiencia siente esperanza.
teaching.explanationEs: Inspire busca emoción positiva; audience es el público que escucha.
segments: A story can inspire: the speaker fails twice, then
finds a way, and the audience feels hope.
teaching.audioText: A story can inspire: the speaker fails twice, then finds a way, and the audience feels hope.

teaching.en: A story can warn, so the speaker shows a mistake and its cost: 'I ignored the noise, and the car stopped on a dark road.'
teaching.es: Una historia puede advertir, así que el narrador muestra un error y su coste: «Ignoré el ruido y el coche se paró en una carretera oscura».
teaching.explanationEs: Warn = avisar de un peligro; lo que importa es el error y su precio.
segments: A story can warn, so the speaker shows a mistake and its cost:
'I ignored the noise, and the car stopped on a dark road.'
teaching.audioText: A story can warn, so the speaker shows a mistake and its cost: 'I ignored the noise, and the car stopped on a dark road.'

teaching.en: A story can persuade because the listener sees the result, not only the argument: 'Our shop nearly closed, then one change saved it.'
teaching.es: Una historia puede convencer porque el oyente ve el resultado, no solo el argumento: «Nuestra tienda casi cierra, hasta que un cambio la salvó».
teaching.explanationEs: Persuade = convencer a alguien de hacer algo.
segments: A story can persuade because the listener sees the result, not only
the argument: 'Our shop nearly closed, then one change saved it.'
teaching.audioText: A story can persuade because the listener sees the result, not only the argument: 'Our shop nearly closed, then one change saved it.'

teaching.en: After the setback, the lesson appears: 'That winter taught me to ask for help.'
teaching.es: Después del revés aparece la lección: «Aquel invierno me enseñó a pedir ayuda».
teaching.explanationEs: Setback es un contratiempo; lesson revela casi siempre el propósito.
segments: After the setback, the lesson appears: 'That
winter taught me to ask for help.'
teaching.audioText: After the setback, the lesson appears: 'That winter taught me to ask for help.'

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito se cuenta esta historia?

choices.text: To warn
To inspire
To persuade

feedback.es: Muestra un error (ignorar el ruido) y su coste, que es lo propio de una historia para advertir.

hint.es: Fíjate en el error y en lo que cuesta.

origin.text: I ignored the noise in the engine for weeks. One night the car stopped on a dark road.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una historia puede inspirar mostrando cómo alguien resolvió un problema.»

feedback.es: Inspire es la palabra de la historia que despierta esperanza al mostrar cómo se supera un problema.

origin.text: A story can ___ the audience by showing how someone solved a problem.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Aquel verano me enseñó una lección.»

answer.text: That summer taught me a lesson

feedback.es: El sujeto es la época, que «enseña» la lección, como en «That winter taught me…».

prompt.es: Elige el momento de la historia que revela su propósito.

choices.text: Our shop was nearly empty.
Now I tell every small business: try something new.
Then we moved online.

feedback.es: La frase final se dirige al público y dice qué debe hacer: ahí se revela el propósito.

origin.text: Our shop was nearly empty. Then we moved online, and in a year we had customers in six countries. Now I tell every small business: try something new.

prompt.es: Escucha esta historia y decide con qué propósito se cuenta.

choices.text: To inspire the audience with a happy ending.
To sell a product to the audience.
To warn the audience about a costly mistake.

feedback.es: El narrador cuenta un error, su coste y termina pidiendo al público que actúe: advierte.

origin.audio: For years I never saved money. Then the roof fell in, and I had nothing. Please, start a small emergency fund today.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada historia breve con su propósito principal.

pairs: The runner who lost twice and won the third time.
The driver who ignored the warning light.
The shop owner whose sales doubled after one change, and who tells you to try it.
A list of dates with no problem and no lesson.

feedback.es: Cada historia destaca algo distinto: superar un revés, pagar un error, mostrar un resultado deseable o nada.

pairs: The runner who lost twice and won the third time.
The driver who ignored the warning light.
The shop owner whose sales doubled after one change, and who tells you to try it.
A list of dates with no problem and no lesson.

prompt.es: Elige el propósito de esta anécdota breve.

choices.text: To persuade the audience to act
To warn about a serious danger
To inspire with a personal failure

prompt.es: Escucha y decide qué busca provocar la historia en la audiencia.

choices.text: Fear of driving on the road.
Hope and courage to try again.
Doubt about the examiner.

feedback.es: El revés se supera en el último intento y la lección final anima a no rendirse.

origin.audio: I failed my driving test three times. I was ready to quit, but my sister said: one more try. On the last try, I passed. Never stop after a setback.

prompt.es: Completa: «Toda historia tiene un arco: situación, problema, giro y desenlace.»

feedback.es: El arco es la forma de la historia, de la situación inicial al desenlace.

origin.text: Every story has an ___: a situation, a problem, a turning point and an outcome.

answer.text: The outcome was better than we expected

feedback.es: Outcome es el desenlace, y la comparación usa «better than».

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase revela que la historia pretende persuadir?

choices.text: We opened at eight every Monday.
The power failed that night.
So if it worked for us, it can work for you.

feedback.es: Se dirige al público y le pide hacer lo mismo: es una frase de persuasión.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la lección que revela el propósito de la historia.

choices.text: Ask for help early.
Buy a boat before a flood.
Never trust your neighbours.

feedback.es: La lección final (aprender a pedir ayuda pronto) es lo que el narrador quiere transmitir.

origin.audio: After the flood, our neighbours came with boats and blankets. Nobody asked for anything. That night I learned to ask for help early.

prompt.es: ¿Qué palabra describe un contratiempo que interrumpe el plan?

choices.text: An outcome
A setback
An audience

feedback.es: Un setback es el revés que rompe la rutina y abre el problema de la historia.

title.es: Subir lo que está en juego

es: Crear tensión en el inicio de una historia contrastando la rutina pasada (used to, would) con una ruptura y lo que está en juego.

teaching.en: The stakes are what the character could lose: a job, a friendship or a home.
teaching.es: Lo que está en juego es lo que el personaje podría perder: un trabajo, una amistad o un hogar.
teaching.explanationEs: Stakes es siempre plural en este sentido: «the stakes are high».
segments: The stakes are what the character could lose:
a job, a friendship or a home.
teaching.audioText: The stakes are what the character could lose: a job, a friendship or a home.

teaching.en: Our routine was simple: we used to open at eight, and we would drink tea before the first customer.
teaching.es: Nuestra rutina era sencilla: solíamos abrir a las ocho y tomábamos té antes del primer cliente.
teaching.explanationEs: Used to y would describen hábitos pasados; would solo con acciones.
segments: Our routine was simple: we used to open at eight,
and we would drink tea before the first customer.
teaching.audioText: Our routine was simple: we used to open at eight, and we would drink tea before the first customer.

teaching.en: Then a letter arrived, and a threat hung over everything we had built.
teaching.es: Entonces llegó una carta y una amenaza se cernió sobre todo lo que habíamos construido.
teaching.explanationEs: Then + pasado simple marca la ruptura de la rutina; threat es la amenaza.
segments: Then a letter arrived, and a threat
hung over everything we had built.
teaching.audioText: Then a letter arrived, and a threat hung over everything we had built.

teaching.en: Now the risk was real: if we failed to pay by Friday, we would lose the shop.
teaching.es: Ahora el riesgo era real: si no pagábamos el viernes, perderíamos la tienda.
teaching.explanationEs: If + pasado, would + verbo base, para el riesgo visto desde el pasado.
segments: Now the risk was real: if we failed to
pay by Friday, we would lose the shop.
teaching.audioText: Now the risk was real: if we failed to pay by Friday, we would lose the shop.

teaching.en: The call did not just disrupt our routine, it filled me with dread.
teaching.es: La llamada no solo alteró nuestra rutina, me llenó de temor.
teaching.explanationEs: Disrupt es alterar algo que funcionaba; dread es un miedo que crece.
segments: The call did not just disrupt our
routine, it filled me with dread.
teaching.audioText: The call did not just disrupt our routine, it filled me with dread.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase expresa una rutina repetida en el pasado?

choices.text: We were opening the shop at eight.
We used to open the shop at eight.
We have opened the shop at eight.

feedback.es: «Used to» expresa un hábito pasado que ya no continúa.

hint.es: Busca el hábito que ya no existe.

prompt.es: Completa: «Solíamos tomar té antes de que llegara el primer cliente.»

feedback.es: Para una acción repetida en el pasado sirven would y used to.

hint.es: Hábito de acción: hay dos formas posibles.

origin.text: We ___ drink tea before the first customer came.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Solíamos cruzar el puente cada día.»

answer.text: We used to cross the bridge every day

feedback.es: «Used to» va seguido del verbo base: cross.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto y «used to».

prompt.es: Elige la reescritura que añade lo que está en juego.

choices.text: I worked in a café and I liked it a lot.
One day a letter came and it was a very long letter.
We used to serve forty customers a day. Then a letter came, and if we failed to pay, we would lose the café.

feedback.es: Incluye rutina, ruptura y riesgo concreto; las otras no dicen qué se puede perder.

origin.text: I worked in a café. One day a letter came.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué amenaza rompe la rutina de esta historia.

choices.text: The river became dirty.
A storm broke their tent.
Their parents moved to another town.

feedback.es: La rutina (nadar y dormir junto al río) se rompe cuando el agua se vuelve negra.

origin.audio: Every summer we would swim in the river, and we used to sleep outside near the water. Then, one morning, the water turned black.

prompt.es: Completa: «Éramos felices en esa casa, pero ahora está vacía.»

feedback.es: Be es un estado, por eso se usa used to y no would.

origin.text: We ___ be happy in that house, but now it is empty.

prompt.es: ¿Qué falta en esta apertura para crear tensión?

choices.text: A longer list of morning habits
What the characters could lose
A second version of the routine

feedback.es: Hay rutina y ruptura, pero no se dice qué se puede perder: faltan las apuestas.

origin.text: We used to walk to school every morning. One day it rained.

prompt.es: Escucha y decide qué teme perder el narrador.

choices.text: His grandfather's boat.
His place at school.
The mornings he shared with his grandfather.

feedback.es: Su temor final es perder las mañanas que pasaba con su abuelo.

origin.audio: My grandfather would wake me at five, and we used to fish until noon. Then the doctor said he could not walk the river path again. I was afraid I would lose our mornings together.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si la carta llegaba tarde, perderíamos la tienda.»

feedback.es: El riesgo se expresa con «if» + pasado y «would» + verbo base.

prompt.es: Escribe un inicio de historia con rutina, amenaza y riesgo.

answer.text: We used to live by the river, and every morning my grandfather and I would go fishing. Then one night the water rose, and dread filled the house. If the wall broke, we would lose everything we owned.
accepted: We used to live by the river, and every morning my grandfather and I would go fishing. Then one night the water rose, and dread filled the house. If the wall broke, we would lose everything we owned.
When I was a child, we would spend every summer by the lake. One day, a letter arrived, and my father's face turned pale. If the bank did not receive the money by Friday, we would lose the house.

origin.text: Datos: vivías junto a un río y cada mañana ibas a pescar con tu abuelo; una noche subió el agua y hubo peligro para la casa. Usa used to o would, pasado simple y un condicional.

prompt.es: En una historia sobre el pasado, ¿qué frase usa mal «would»?

choices.text: We would be happy in that house.
We would race the ferry every morning.
We would drink tea before work.

feedback.es: Would no expresa estados del pasado como ser feliz: ahí hay que usar used to.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué está en juego en la historia.

choices.text: Their school uniforms.
Their friendships with classmates.
Their football trophies.

feedback.es: Si el colegio cierra, los niños perderían a sus amigos: eso es lo que está en juego.

origin.audio: We used to play in the school yard every day. Then the town hall announced that it would close the school. If it closed, we would lose our friends.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Un día llegó una carta y todo cambió.»

answer.text: One day a letter came and everything changed

feedback.es: La ruptura se marca con «one day» y el pasado simple.

es: Localizar en un relato oído el fondo habitual, el giro, la reacción, la consecuencia y la reflexión.

teaching.en: The background shows the habit before the change: 'We used to eat dinner together every night.'
teaching.es: El fondo muestra el hábito anterior al cambio: «Solíamos cenar juntos todas las noches».
teaching.explanationEs: Background = lo que ocurría antes: suele usar used to, would o pasado continuo.
segments: The background shows the habit before the change:
'We used to eat dinner together every night.'
teaching.audioText: The background shows the habit before the change: 'We used to eat dinner together every night.'

teaching.en: A twist is a change nobody expects, and words like 'until' and 'suddenly' often announce it.
teaching.es: Un giro es un cambio que nadie espera, y palabras como «until» y «suddenly» suelen anunciarlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Until y suddenly funcionan como señal de que algo va a cambiar.
segments: A twist is a change nobody expects, and
words like 'until' and 'suddenly' often announce it.
teaching.audioText: A twist is a change nobody expects, and words like 'until' and 'suddenly' often announce it.

teaching.en: The shift usually comes with a signal like 'until one evening' or 'but then'.
teaching.es: El cambio suele llegar con una señal como «hasta que una noche» o «pero entonces».
teaching.explanationEs: Shift es el paso de la rutina al suceso; escucha la señal.
segments: The shift usually comes with a signal
like 'until one evening' or 'but then'.
teaching.audioText: The shift usually comes with a signal like 'until one evening' or 'but then'.

teaching.en: The reaction tells us how the character felt: 'I froze and my hands started to shake.'
teaching.es: La reacción nos dice cómo se sintió el personaje: «Me quedé helado y me empezaron a temblar las manos».
teaching.explanationEs: Reaction = lo que siente o hace justo después del giro.
segments: The reaction tells us how the character felt:
'I froze and my hands started to shake.'
teaching.audioText: The reaction tells us how the character felt: 'I froze and my hands started to shake.'

teaching.en: The consequence is what changed afterwards: 'Since that night, we have eaten at different times.'
teaching.es: La consecuencia es lo que cambió después: «Desde aquella noche, hemos cenado a horas distintas».
teaching.explanationEs: Consequence suele ir con since y el presente perfecto.
segments: The consequence is what changed afterwards: 'Since that
night, we have eaten at different times.'
teaching.audioText: The consequence is what changed afterwards: 'Since that night, we have eaten at different times.'

teaching.en: The reflection closes the story with meaning: 'Looking back, I realise it saved us.'
teaching.es: La reflexión cierra la historia con sentido: «Mirando atrás, me doy cuenta de que nos salvó».
teaching.explanationEs: Reflection es la idea final; «looking back» es su señal más frecuente.
segments: The reflection closes the story with meaning:
'Looking back, I realise it saved us.'
teaching.audioText: The reflection closes the story with meaning: 'Looking back, I realise it saved us.'

prompt.es: ¿Qué palabra señala el giro de la historia?

choices.text: together
every
until

feedback.es: «Until» anuncia que la rutina se rompe en ese momento.

hint.es: Anuncia el cambio respecto a la rutina.

origin.text: We used to eat dinner together every night, until one evening the phone rang.

prompt.es: Completa: «La consecuencia nos dice qué cambió después.»

feedback.es: Consequence es lo que cambia después del giro.

hint.es: Es la pieza que sigue a la reacción.

The narrator's father stayed at home because he lost his job.
The family had breakfast together.

feedback.es: El giro llega tras «Until one day»: el padre se queda en casa porque perdió su trabajo.

origin.audio: Every morning my father would leave for work at six, and we rarely saw him. Until one day he stayed at home. He said he had lost his job. I hugged him, and for the first time in years, we had breakfast together. Looking back, I think that day was a gift.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de esta historia con la pieza que representa.

Looking back, I prefer the train anyway.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una función: hábito anterior, suceso inesperado, emoción, efecto duradero y balance final.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la reflexión final de la narradora.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que funciona como reflexión final de una anécdota.

choices.text: Suddenly the phone rang in the kitchen.

teaching.en: Open with a marker like 'In those days' and describe the habit: 'In those days, we would walk to school together.'

segments: Open with a marker like 'In those days' and describe the

teaching.audioText: Open with a marker like 'In those days' and describe the habit: 'In those days, we would walk to school together.'

teaching.en: Gradually, small things changed, and the reader began to feel that something was wrong.
teaching.es: Poco a poco, pequeñas cosas cambiaron y el lector empezó a sentir que algo iba mal.

teaching.audioText: Gradually, small things changed, and the reader began to feel that something was wrong.

teaching.audioText: Meanwhile, my brother was fixing the boat, unaware of what was coming.

teaching.audioText: To build suspense, delay the important detail: 'I opened the door, and then I saw...'

teaching.audioText: Reveal the twist in one short sentence: 'The door was already open.'

teaching.audioText: Eventually, she told me everything, and the room went silent.

prompt.es: Escribe una anécdota de 160 a 210 palabras con hábito, giro y consecuencia.

answer.text: In those days, my grandfather and I used to fish at the lake every Sunday. He would bring a bottle of tea, and we would sit in silence for hours. Gradually, I noticed that his hands were shaking, but he never mentioned it. Meanwhile, I was busy with school and my friends, and I did not ask any questions. One Sunday, he did not come to the door. I waited for twenty minutes, and my hands were cold. Then I saw the light in the kitchen. He was sitting at the table, pale and quiet, with our fishing things beside him. 'I cannot walk to the lake any more,' he said. I froze. I had never seen him sad. Eventually, I sat next to him, and we drank the tea together, without fishing. Since that day, I have visited him every Sunday, and we talk instead of fishing. Looking back, I think that quiet morning taught me more than all our years at the lake.
accepted: In those days, my grandfather and I used to fish at the lake every Sunday. He would bring a bottle of tea, and we would sit in silence for hours. Gradually, I noticed that his hands were shaking, but he never mentioned it. Meanwhile, I was busy with school and my friends, and I did not ask any questions. One Sunday, he did not come to the door. I waited for twenty minutes, and my hands were cold. Then I saw the light in the kitchen. He was sitting at the table, pale and quiet, with our fishing things beside him. 'I cannot walk to the lake any more,' he said. I froze. I had never seen him sad. Eventually, I sat next to him, and we drank the tea together, without fishing. Since that day, I have visited him every Sunday, and we talk instead of fishing. Looking back, I think that quiet morning taught me more than all our years at the lake.

In those days, I would walk home along the river every evening, after my classes. Gradually, the path became darker, because the lights went out one by one. Meanwhile, I was thinking about my exam and I did not notice the silence. Then I heard steps behind me. My heart stopped. I turned around slowly, and I saw a small dog with a red bottle in its mouth. Eventually, I laughed so much that I had to sit down. Since that night, I always carry some bread in my pocket, just in case. Looking back, I think that night taught me to laugh at my own fear.

feedback.es: La anécdota combina fondo habitual, marcadores de secuencia, un giro con suspense, la consecuencia y una reflexión final.

title.es: Una historia que vale la pena repetir

es: Construir y contar una historia con gancho, conflicto, resolución y una idea final, y responder a dos preguntas de un oyente.

teaching.en: A story people want to retell starts with a hook: 'I got on the wrong train, and it changed everything.'
teaching.es: Una historia que la gente quiere volver a contar empieza con un gancho: «Me subí al tren equivocado y lo cambió todo».
teaching.explanationEs: Retell = contar de nuevo; el gancho despierta curiosidad en la primera frase.
segments: A story people want to retell starts with a hook:
'I got on the wrong train, and it changed everything.'
teaching.audioText: A story people want to retell starts with a hook: 'I got on the wrong train, and it changed everything.'

teaching.en: The conflict is the problem the character cannot ignore: the train was heading for a city I did not know.
teaching.es: El conflicto es el problema que el personaje no puede ignorar: el tren iba hacia una ciudad que yo no conocía.
teaching.explanationEs: Conflict = el problema central.
segments: The conflict is the problem the character cannot ignore: the
train was heading for a city I did not know.
teaching.audioText: The conflict is the problem the character cannot ignore: the train was heading for a city I did not know.

teaching.en: The resolution shows how the problem ended: 'A stranger shared her map, and I found my way.'
teaching.es: La resolución muestra cómo terminó el problema: «Una desconocida compartió su mapa y encontré mi camino».
teaching.explanationEs: Resolution = el desenlace del conflicto.

shared her map, and I found my way.'
teaching.audioText: The resolution shows how the problem ended: 'A stranger shared her map, and I found my way.'

teaching.en: Add one vivid detail, such as the smell of oranges on the platform, so the listener can see the scene.

teaching.explanationEs: Un solo detalle vivid vale más que cinco generales.

prompt.es: Cuenta una historia familiar con gancho, conflicto, resolución e idea final.

answer.text: Fifty years ago, my grandmother missed the last bus the night before her wedding. She was alone on a dark road, and it started to rain. Then a farmer stopped and offered her a lift. She arrived at dawn, tired and muddy, but she reached the church on time. The lesson? Sometimes help comes from the people you least expect. Was she worried? Terribly, but she kept walking. Did he wait for her? Of course! My grandfather was standing at the church door, and they stayed together for fifty years.
accepted: Fifty years ago, my grandmother missed the last bus the night before her wedding. She was alone on a dark road, and it started to rain. Then a farmer stopped and offered her a lift. She arrived at dawn, tired and muddy, but she reached the church on time. The lesson? Sometimes help comes from the people you least expect. Was she worried? Terribly, but she kept walking. Did he wait for her? Of course! My grandfather was standing at the church door, and they stayed together for fifty years.

My grandmother always tells us about the night before her wedding. She missed the last bus, and she had to walk in the rain. Suddenly, a farmer stopped his car and gave her a lift, so she got home at dawn. Was she worried? Yes, but she kept calm. Did he wait for her? Of course! My grandfather was at the church door that same morning. The takeaway is simple: people can surprise you when you need them.

feedback.es: La historia tiene gancho, conflicto (perder el bus), resolución (el granjero), idea final y respuestas a las dos preguntas del oyente.

origin.text: Datos: tu abuela perdió el último autobús la noche antes de su boda; un granjero la llevó en su coche; llegó al amanecer, cansada y con barro. Un oyente pregunta: «Was she worried?» y «Did he wait for her?». Responde a ambas dentro del texto y cierra con una idea final.
